hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/game/gamemain DoWorldAnimation 0x5c:0x95 --raw --diff - if the emission ORDER of the four definitions differs between the streams, the residual is a schedule fact and the pair-exchange framing is wrong. Measured 2026-09-03 over the whole body: both streams emit `addi <base>,r3,@gWorldInfo` at +0x60, `addi <count>,<base>,144` at +0x64, `li <track>,0` at +0x8c and `li <data>,0` at +0x90, in that order, with identical opcodes - so emission order is IDENTICAL and only the register numbers differ, which is what makes this an assignment question.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - all six callee-saved first definitions, the stmw/lmw base (r26 in both), the frame size (32 in both), every loop-carried use at +0xac/+0xb0/+0xc0/+0xc8/+0xd4/+0xd8/+0xdc and the emission order of the four definitions were read from the aligned raw view against the retail bytes over the whole 63-instruction body, in HEAD and in each of the three probes.
hypothesis.statement: The residual is a clean two-pair exchange and the pairs are internally correct in both streams, which is the whole diagnosis. Every register below is quoted from its DEFINING instruction in the aligned raw view, ours against target at the same offset. The gWorldInfo base: ours `@0x60 addi r31,r3,0 @gWorldInfo(ADDR16_LO)` against target `@0x60 addi r29,r3,0 @gWorldInfo(ADDR16_LO)`. The &nworldanims pointer: ours `@0x64 addi r30,r31,144` against target `@0x64 addi r28,r29,144`. The track_off induction pointer: ours `@0x8c li r29,0` against target `@0x8c li r31,0`. The data_off induction pointer: ours `@0x90 li r28,0` against target `@0x90 li r30,0`. So ours assigns, descending: {base, count} = {r31, r30} then {track_off, data_off} = {r29, r28}; retail assigns {track_off, data_off} = {r31, r30} then {base, count} = {r29, r28}. The loop counter agrees, ours and target both `@0x84 li r27,0`, and so does anim_base, both `@0x80 lwz r26,12(r3)`. Neither pair is reachable by declaration order - probe (c) proved the count/base pair is compiler-generated from the expressions, not from the declared local, and probe (a) proved the data_off/track_off pair sits in a different allocation class from count/header. The untried axis is therefore STATEMENT order, not declaration order: our block writes `count = &gWorldInfo.nworldanims; header = ...; anim_base = header[3]; i = 0; data_off = NULL; track_off = NULL;` and the two `li 0` land at +0x8c/+0x90, AFTER the base and count pointers are materialised at +0x60/+0x64. The idea is to write the two induction pointers' initialisations FIRST in the block and see whether the pair that is created first is the pair that takes the top of the range - which is what our stream does today, and is the opposite of retail's, so the prediction is falsifiable in one build.
